openClinicalQuestions: Which Indian society or FOGSI timing thresholds (if any) should be cited alongside ASRM for local readers?
Does Dr. Charmi want male-factor ‘up to about half of couples’ epidemiology quoted, or keep to ‘semen analysis early’ without percentages?

claimLedger.claim: Evaluate at 12 months if female partner <35, at 6 months if ≥35; more immediate if >40; no delay with known infertility-related conditions; include semen evaluation; parallel male evaluation when applicable
claimLedger.sourceSection: ASRM · Fertility evaluation of infertile women: a committee opinion (2026) · 2026 committee opinion (Fertil Steril DOI listed by ASRM)
claimLedger.limitations: US society opinion; local referral pathways in India may use different service names

claimLedger.claim: Ovarian reserve tests reflect oocyte quantity not quality; should not be used as a fertility test for women with unproven fertility
claimLedger.sourceSection: ASRM · Testing and interpreting measures of ovarian reserve: a committee opinion (2020) · 2020 committee opinion
claimLedger.limitations: Does not replace age-based counselling; weak link to pregnancy outcomes

claimLedger.claim: RPL defined as two or more pregnancy losses; excludes ectopic and molar pregnancy
claimLedger.sourceSection: ESHRE · Guideline on recurrent pregnancy loss (2022 update / Jan 2023 version) · Issued / updated material dated January 2023 on ESHRE site
claimLedger.limitations: European society definition; some older local protocols still used three losses

claimLedger.claim: Do not use AMH as a predictor of clinical pregnancy through spontaneous conception
claimLedger.sourceSection: NICE · NG257 investigation of fertility problems — ovarian reserve testing · Published 31 March 2026
claimLedger.limitations: UK guidance; AMH still used for counselling about ovarian response in assisted conception
